title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Named UIUC places for collaboration, recreation, making, and outdoor breaks, backed by current public university sources.

cards.title: Grainger Engineering Library
cards.subtitle: Engineering Quad study space
cards.notes: Choose the lower level for group work or head upstairs for a quieter session. Use the library’s space guide to match your work to each floor.
cards.short_summary: A multi-floor engineering library with distinct settings for collaborative and quiet work.
cards.evidence_claim: Grainger Engineering Library’s study-space guide identifies lower-level group and collaborative seating, plus quieter upper-floor study areas.
cards.access_notes: Consult the library’s current hours and space guidance before visiting.

cards.title: IDEA Lab
cards.subtitle: Grainger Library basement
cards.notes: Reserve a room or seat for a hands-on project, then check in with your i-card. Review the Lab’s current closure and reservation notices first.
cards.short_summary: A technology-rich collaboration center for making, media, and project work.
cards.evidence_claim: The IDEA Lab is a collaborative technology center in Grainger Library with reservable spaces; its policies require a valid i-card or Illinois App for entry.
cards.access_notes: Access is for UIUC-affiliated patrons and may be by appointment; a valid i-card or Illinois App is required.

cards.title: The Orange Room
cards.subtitle: Main Library, rooms 100 and 112
cards.notes: Set up at a large table for a group task, or reserve a study room. The space also has short-term technology loans from its service desk.
cards.short_summary: A Main Library study hub designed for both individual and group work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Orange Room has large study tables, reservable study rooms, short-term technology loans, and supports group and individual study.
cards.access_notes: Study-room availability and technology-loan eligibility are governed by current library policies.

cards.title: Media Commons Collaborative Space
cards.subtitle: Main Library, Room 220
cards.notes: Use the collaboration rooms, scanners, or desktop stations for media-heavy coursework. Check Room 220’s schedule, since its hours differ from Room 306.
cards.short_summary: A Main Library media workspace with collaboration rooms, scanners, and computers.
cards.evidence_claim: Media Commons Room 220 includes collaboration rooms, scanners, desktop computers, docking stations, and posted room-specific hours.
cards.access_notes: Room 220 operates on its own posted schedule; hours may be reduced during breaks and summer.

cards.title: Funk ACES Library
cards.subtitle: 1101 S. Goodwin Avenue
cards.notes: Reserve a group room for a planned class project, or use open seating for a quieter work block. Bring your NetID if you need an online reservation.
cards.short_summary: An ACES library with open study seating and six reservable group rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Funk ACES Library lists 350 seats and six reservable study rooms; students reserve group rooms through the online system using an Illinois NetID.
cards.source_title: Room Reservations in Funk ACES Library
cards.access_notes: Online group-room reservations require an Illinois NetID and password; unreserved rooms may be first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Illini Union
cards.subtitle: 1401 W. Green Street
cards.notes: Use the Union as a campus meeting point, then check its events calendar or request an interview or study room when you need a defined space.
cards.short_summary: The student union combines study areas, student organizations, programs, and reservable space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Illini Union houses study spaces, student organizations, programs and activities, and offers interview and study-room requests.
cards.source_title: Illini Union at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
cards.access_notes: Event and room access depend on availability and the Union’s current reservation procedures.

cards.title: Activities & Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: 201 E. Peabody Drive
cards.notes: Plan a workout, swim, court session, or climbing visit around the facility schedule. Confirm that your current membership and ID allow entry.
cards.short_summary: A Campus Recreation facility with courts, pools, fitness areas, and a climbing wall.
cards.evidence_claim: The ARC lists courts, indoor and outdoor pools, fitness areas, a climbing wall, and access for current students, members, and guests.
cards.access_notes: Facility entry requires valid identification and an eligible Campus Recreation membership or visitor status.

cards.title: University of Illinois Arboretum
cards.subtitle: 1800 S. Lincoln Avenue, Urbana
cards.notes: Take a daylight walk through the gardens and natural areas, keeping to paths and posted rules. Use the visit page for directions and weather-aware planning.
cards.short_summary: A 100-plus-acre collection of campus gardens and natural spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arboretum comprises more than 100 acres of gardens and natural spaces, is open daily from sunrise to sunset, and has free admission.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset; outdoor access is weather-dependent.

cards.title: Japan House
cards.subtitle: Near the Arboretum on South Lincoln Avenue
cards.notes: Walk the garden paths respectfully and consult Japan House’s visitor update before going. The tea garden is presently closed for annex construction.
cards.short_summary: A campus teaching facility surrounded by Japanese-style gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: Japan House is surrounded by Japanese gardens and directs visitors to stroll the gardens; its tea garden is currently closed for construction.
cards.source_title: Visiting the Gardens at Japan House
cards.access_notes: Follow garden etiquette and construction signage; the tea garden is currently closed.

cards.title: Noel Welcome Garden
cards.subtitle: University of Illinois Arboretum
cards.notes: Start an Arboretum walk at the northern path, pausing at the trellis, crabapples, and hydrangeas. Keep the visit low-impact and stay on marked paths.
cards.short_summary: A named Arboretum garden and gathering place at the northern path entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Noel Welcome Garden is the first garden on the Arboretum’s northern path and is described by the Arboretum as a gathering place for visitors.
cards.access_notes: The garden is within the Arboretum, which is open daily from sunrise to sunset.
